transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I just… I’ve been feeling really low most days. Like I’m stuck at the bottom of some dark hole, and even when I’m around people, it doesn’t really lift. It just feels heavy… kind of hopeless.
How long have you been feeling this low?
About… a year and a couple months. Since last fall, after I got hurt on that HVAC job. My back and then… things just kind of unraveled after that.
Does your low mood feel mainly caused by what happened after your injury?
Yeah… I guess it started after that. It’s been about a year and two months now, since I fell on that HVAC job and hurt my back. After that, everything just kind of… came apart.
Before this injury happened, had you already been feeling depressed for years?
No… not for years before. It really started after the fall, about a year and two months ago, when I hurt my back on that HVAC job. After that, things just… unraveled.
If your life had gone back to normal after the injury, do you think you would still be feeling this depressed?
I don’t know… maybe not this bad. But now most days it just feels like I’m stuck down in this dark hole, and even being around people doesn’t really lift it. It’s just… heavy. Hopeless.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I have. I used to like hiking, painting, going to the makerspace, that kind of thing. Even figuring out a hard install used to feel good. Now I just… stare at the supplies or don’t answer people’s calls. It doesn’t feel worth starting.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge a lot?
I’m not sure… I mean, I get tense sometimes, but I don’t really know if I’d call it anxious a lot.
If your injury and the problems that came after it were fully resolved tomorrow, do you think you would still feel depressed?

I… I don’t know. Maybe some of it would lift, but this heaviness feels like it’s just there most days. Like I’m still down in that hole, even around people. It’s hard to imagine just waking up and not feeling hopeless.
Before the fall on the HVAC job, had you ever had another period in your life when you felt this depressed for weeks at a time?
I don’t really know. I’ve had rough times before, I guess, but… I don’t think I can say it was like this. Not for weeks like this, no.
Do you feel depressed even when you’re not thinking about the injury or the problems that came after it?
Yeah… I think so. Even when I’m not thinking about all that, most days it’s like I’m down in a dark hole. I can be around people I know and still feel heavy… hopeless, I guess.
Have you been having thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Yeah… I have. I don’t really like saying it, but sometimes I think maybe everybody would be better off if I just didn’t wake up.

And when the pain and the money stuff all piles up… I catch myself thinking about ending it. It scares me.
Have you made a specific plan to end your life?
I… I don’t have, like, a set plan. It’s more these thoughts that come when everything piles up—pain, money… thinking people might be better off if I didn’t wake up. It scares me.
Before your injury, was there ever a time in your life when you felt this depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?
No… not like this. This has really been going on since the fall at the HVAC job… about a year and two months now. After my back got hurt, everything just kind of unraveled.
Over the past several months, have you felt anxious or worried much of the time?
I mean… I don’t know. I worry about things, sure, but I’m not sure I’d say anxious all the time. It’s hard to tell.
Have you had trouble sleeping?

Yeah… sleep’s been pretty messed up. Some nights I’m just lying there for hours, my back hurting and my mind going over bills. Other times I sleep way too long and still wake up feeling like I didn’t rest at all.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
Yeah… I have. Stuff I used to do without thinking, like paperwork or repair diagrams, it all kind of runs together now. I’ll just sit there stuck, not even able to pick which form to open first.
Do you feel like your depression is stronger than you would expect just from the injury and the problems it caused?

Yeah… I think so. The injury made things hard, but this feels bigger than that. Most days it’s like I’m stuck down in some dark place, even around people I know. I just feel… heavy. Hopeless, I guess.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?

Yeah… it’s changed. I don’t really eat normal anymore. Some days it’s just coffee most of the day because food makes me feel kind of sick, and then later at night I’ll pick at whatever’s around… not really enjoying it.
During this past year, was there a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly every day?
Yeah… there’s been more than two weeks. Honestly, most days I feel like I’m just sitting at the bottom of a dark hole. Even around people I know, I can’t really shake that heavy, hopeless feeling.
Before your injury, did you ever have another period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly every day?
I… I’m not really sure. I don’t think I can pin down anything like that before the injury. It’s hard to say.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a current depressive episode lasting about 14 months with persistent depressed mood, marked anhedonia, sleep disturbance, appetite change, impaired concentration, hopelessness, and suicidal ideation. Although symptoms began after a significant psychosocial/medical stressor (work injury with pain and financial strain), the patient reports the depression feels more severe than expected from the stressor and persists even when not focused on it, supporting a depressive episode rather than adjustment disorder. There is no clear evidence of prior distinct depressive episodes, making recurrent depressive disorder less supported, and anxiety symptoms are insufficiently prominent for mixed anxiety and depressive disorder.
